subject: Renewal structure and staged ramp proposal for OliveTech
messages:
From: Sara White <sara.white@olivetech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal - upcoming term and capacity update

Hi Irene,

Hope you9re well. Our current agreement with Redwood is coming up for renewal in November and the product team has flagged a need to rework the term structure. We9re seeing faster-than-expected usage growth and want to discuss: a multi-year commitment option, a staged ramp that matches our product launch schedule, and the ability to opt out of auto-renew in year two if growth shifts.

High-level asks:
- Example 2- or 3-year pricing with staged token buckets
- Co-terming our different projects onto a single renewal date (if possible)
- Any operational changes needed for billing cadence or reserved capacity

Can we set a 30-minute call next week? If you have a short strawman proposal, please share before the call so I can loop finance and procurement.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara White
Head of Platform Product
OliveTech

[External attachment referenced: procurement_schedule_q4.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@olivetech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-09-30T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal - upcoming term and capacity update

Thanks Sara 83; great to hear from you. We9ve reviewed your usage pattern and I think we can put together a structure that balances cost predictability with the ability to scale in-line with your launch. Sketch below is what I9d propose as a starting point (we9ll attach a brief workplan and SOW for details).

Proposed approach (strawman):
- Term: 24 months (option to extend to 36 months for additional discount)
- Ramp schedule: three tranches synced to your product milestones (Q1 ramp 30%, Q2 additional 40%, Q3 remaining 30%)
- Co-terming: collapse existing project-level renewals into a single co-term date at renewal close; we can prorate mid-cycle for any remaining credit
- Auto-renew: default ON, but include an explicit opt-out window (60 days before renewal) and an amendment path for early exit with short-notice true-up
- Billing cadence: quarterly invoices, with an optional annual prepay for up to 6% additional discount

Next steps I recommend:
1) Karthik will send a pricing workbook showing the tiered commit and per-token effective cost across the ramp.
2) We9ll attach a two-page operational workplan for co-terming and cutover (ops runbook, data migration notes for billing).
3) If this matches your expectations, we9ll prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment and a quick SOW for the staged capacity onboarding.

I9ve attached the workplan and SOW draft for review. Quick question: do you want the ramp percentages locked (fixed buckets) or flexible with a usage true-up? Your procurement preference will change the recommended credit/discount structure.

Best,
Irene
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: 20280930-olive-Renewal-Bridge-Workplan.pdf (PDF, 312KB)]
[Attachment: olive_renewal_sow.xlsx (Excel, 76KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara White <sara.white@olivetech.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal - upcoming term and capacity update

Sara 83; attaching the detailed pricing workbook as discussed. Highlights:
- 24-month plan: 12% blended discount vs. current list when using the staged ramp (payments quarterly).
- 36-month option: additional 3% discount, but requires annual usage true-up.
- Flexible bucket option: keeps lower initial commitment and treats overage as pay-as-you-go with a capped unit price; this reduces upfront discount but gives flexibility.

Attached tabs: Executive summary (summary numbers), Ramp schedule (quarterly buckets), Billing cadence examples, Amendment language excerpt.

DocuSign link (example amendment): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/123456789
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-OT-2028-0912

If procurement prefers locked buckets we can show the true-up math explicitly. If you prefer the flexible approach, we9ll propose a higher per-token floor and a smaller committed discount.

Irene 83; cc9d you on the workbook so you can confirm the operational notes before we produce a final amendment.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: olive_renewal_pricing_workbook.xlsx (Excel, 214KB)]

From: Sara White <sara.white@olivetech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: OliveTech Finance <billing@olivetech.com>
Date: 2028-10-03T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal - upcoming term and capacity update

Thanks Karthik and Irene 83; this is helpful. Quick internal update from my side:
- Product is aligned with the 24-month staged ramp but asks that the buckets be slightly front-loaded (45% / 35% / 20%) to account for launch spikes.
- Procurement is leaning toward locked buckets for budget certainty, but finance wants the option to change billing cadence to annual prepay if we can get the additional discount.
- Two asks before we sign: 1) a one-page amendment summary that explicitly calls out the opt-out window and true-up math, and 2) a short operational checklist for the co-term cutover so our billing team can plan.

Can you send the one-page amendment summary and an ops checklist? Finance is asking for a 14-day review window, so a target close by 2028-10-17 would be ideal. We9ll review the workbook this week and get back with any redlines.

Thanks,
Sara
